q1.title: Can supply cover additional data-center demand?
q1.verdict: The announced demand is a large share of the margin and would require additional firm supply.
q1.stat: 1,500 MW forecast by 2028 vs a 3,629 MW May 2026 system margin
q1.blurb: DICT's 2028 forecast alone equals 41% of the whole system's May margin, and Meralco has committed 1,000 MW for 10 data centers. A data center is near-flat 24/7 load. IEMOP dispatch schedules recorded load curtailed on 120 grid days in this archive window (7,699.6 MWh). Headroom for added demand of this size requires new supply that is available when needed.
q1.src: IEMOP May 2026 report; PCIJ (Meralco commitment); DICT forecast via BusinessWorld; IEMOP RTD regional summaries

q2.title: Where can new demand connect?
q2.verdict: Public records name the grid limits. New sites behind those limits face the same constraint.
q2.stat: 84 distinct pieces of equipment (99 monitored constraints) hit limits across the real-time and day-ahead runs on 128 archive days; the Leyte-Luzon HVDC ran at max or offline 69% of Dec 2025
q2.blurb: The inter-island links and named 230 kV lines already reach their limits often; the table names the affected equipment. Nearly every announced data-center megawatt sits on Luzon, which already supplies power south over those links. One Sual unit (647 MW) equals 18% of the May system margin. Luzon scheduled reserves fell below the stated requirement in at least one 5-minute interval on 76 of the window's days.
q2.src: IEMOP congestions-manifesting files; IEMOP Dec 2025 report; IEMOP outage schedules

q3.title: How does added demand affect prices?
q3.verdict: Regional prices respond each day. Retail bills reflect the monthly purchase mix.
q3.stat: May 2026: P7.79/kWh system (+38.5% vs April); Luzon P7.02, Visayas P10.2, Mindanao P9.28
q3.blurb: Regional prices can separate when an inter-grid link reaches its limit. While WESM ran administered prices (through 2026-05-01), the three grids stayed within P0.015/kWh of each other; once trading resumed the mean daily high-to-low spread across the three grids was P5.29/kWh. Widest daily regional spread in the archive: P15.722/kWh on 2026-06-08. WESM passes into the Meralco generation charge monthly, and only on the share of energy actually bought on the spot market: June paid P7.0281/kWh for the 10% it drew from WESM, about P0.70/kWh of the P9.0704/kWh generation charge. The rest is contracted and does not move with the spot price. New flat 24/7 load raises the demand the market clears against in every interval.
q3.src: IEMOP monthly reports; archived LWAP files; Meralco June 2026 advisory
